violations.why: ISR can overwrite m between main's assignment and its dereference at line 37, so main reads m and gets the ISR's pointer to a local that is out of scope.
ISR changes m between the two loads of m in main's consecutive dereferences, so line 38 uses a different pointer from line 37.
ISR reads *p between main's two writes to local_var1 and sees the intermediate value 2 instead of the final value.
